setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Git responds with a version number

setupSteps.title: Install Node LTS
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Node responds with a version number

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.verifierLabel: Terminal is open

steps.title: Check Git and Node
steps.body: Use Terminal. Simplicity needs Node 24+ and an Apple Silicon Mac.
steps.verifierLabel: Git works and Node is 24 or newer

steps.title: Install Yarn
steps.body: Simplicity's lockfile is a Yarn one.
steps.verifierLabel: Yarn responds with a version number

expect.prompt: Does the Terminal window show that "npm install -g yarn" finished — an npm summary line such as "added 1 package", with the prompt back and no error?

hints: npm can sit silent for a few seconds while it fetches Yarn from the registry; that is not a failure.
If npm refuses for lack of permission, reinstall Node from nodejs.org rather than re-running this with more privileges.

steps.title: Copy Simplicity to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d Simplicity/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/Simplicity.git
fi
steps.verifierLabel: A Simplicity folder appears

steps.title: Open the Simplicity folder
steps.verifierLabel: Your terminal prompt is inside the Simplicity folder

steps.title: Use the reviewed version
steps.verifierLabel: Git reports the reviewed commit

expect.prompt: Does the Terminal window show a line beginning "HEAD is now at 9e876be"?

hints: "You are in 'detached HEAD' state" is exactly what this command is meant to print — it is not an error.
If Git says the pathspec did not match, the previous `cd Simplicity` did not happen — run it first.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.verifierLabel: The install finishes without an error

expect.prompt: Does the Terminal window show Yarn's final "Done in ..." line with the prompt back, rather than a progress bar still moving?

hints: A fresh clone downloads Electron and the rest of the toolchain; several minutes is normal.
If it stops on a network error, run `yarn install` again — it keeps everything it already downloaded.

steps.title: Build the app
steps.verifierLabel: A Simplicity .dmg appears in the release folder

expect.prompt: Does the Terminal window show electron-builder finished and wrote a .dmg, with the prompt back and no error?

hints: This rebuilds the whole app before it packages it, so several minutes is normal.
The finished Simplicity-mac-arm64.dmg lands in the release folder inside the Simplicity folder.

steps.title: Put Simplicity in Applications
steps.body: Copy the freshly built app into Applications so it's a real, launchable Mac app.
steps.verifierLabel: Simplicity.app is in your Applications folder

steps.title: Open Simplicity
steps.body: Built on your own machine, so macOS opens it without any warning.
steps.verifierLabel: Simplicity opens

steps.title: Let the search engine download
steps.body: About 150 MB, once. Every search then runs on your own machine.
steps.verifierLabel: Simplicity reaches its setup screen

expect.prompt: Has Simplicity moved past the dark splash screen with the spinner to a screen that says "Welcome to Simplicity" or "Choose a provider"?

hints: The status line reads "Setting up local search — this is a one-time download of about 150 MB". It is downloading, not stuck.
If an error dialog appears instead, it names the log file that says why.

steps.title: Choose where answers come from
steps.body: Install Ollama for free local models, or paste an API key you own.
steps.verifierLabel: A provider is connected in Simplicity

steps.title: Ask it one real question
steps.body: Type a question into Simplicity's search box and send it.
steps.verifierLabel: An answer appears with its sources cited

expect.prompt: Is Simplicity showing an answer to a question along with its list of cited sources, rather than an empty search box?

hints: Answers need a provider connected — that is the setup screen from a few steps ago.
